The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada 1 , 2 , 3 . Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ 18 O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive ε Hf ( t ) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta 2 , the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin 4 . Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

articles.title_orig: China seeks 'tangible progress' in ties with US as top diplomat Wang speaks to Rubio ahead of APEC summit
articles.title_zh: China seeks 'tangible progress' in ties with US as top diplomat Wang speaks to Rubio ahead of APEC summit
articles.content_orig:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke by telephone Wednesday with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, emphasizing Beijing's desire to achieve "tangible progress" in relations ahead of upcoming multilateral leader gatherings.
"China is ready to strengthen communication and cooperation with the US side, properly handle differences and sensitive issues," Wang told Rubio, according to China's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning.
Beijing and Washington support each other in the "successful hosting" of the APEC Summit and the G20 Leaders’ Summit, and "work for tangible progress in building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability," said Wang.
Wang affirmed that China's broader policy toward Washington remains "stable and consistent" as both powers prepare for senior diplomatic engagements.
Chins said the call was "positive and constructive."
"Stable momentum of China-US ties did not come easily and is the two major countries' rational choice based on respective and common interests," said Wang, according to a statement by the Foreign Ministry.
The call comes as Chinese President Xi Jinping prepares to host regional heads of state for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting from Nov. 18 - 19 in China. The summit will gather representatives from 21 member economies, including US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, amid reports of a potential trilateral meeting involving Putin in Shenzhen.
Xi and Trump, during their two summits this year in Beijing and Washington, have agreed to build a "constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity," according to China.
The US State Department had not released a readout of the call as of 10.50 am Washington time (1550GMT).

articles.title_orig: US postpones ‘million-dollar’ China ship tax until January
articles.title_zh: US postpones ‘million-dollar’ China ship tax until January
articles.content_orig:
The United States has extended the suspension of port fees targeting China-linked shipping for another two months, keeping the measures on hold through January 9, 2027, according to a notice published Tuesday in the Federal Register.
The decision gives Washington and Beijing additional time to negotiate over Chinese policies affecting the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding industries.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative said the extension took effect November 9 and runs through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 9. It follows a one-year suspension that began November 10, 2025, under a trade agreement announced by President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The pause also continues to cover additional duties on Chinese ship-to-shore cranes and other cargo-handling equipment specified in the agency’s earlier action.
China also extended its suspension of reciprocal port fees on U.S.-linked vessels until January 10.
USTR said the circumstances supporting the original suspension remain in place and that further discussions with China are needed.
The U.S. fees could amount to millions of dollars for a single vessel’s visit. A 50,000-net ton ship, for example, would owe $2.5 million in charges.
The measures arose from the U.S. investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 into China’s targeting of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors for dominance. The suspended fee categories include charges affecting Chinese-owned or operated vessels, Chinese-built vessels and foreign-built vehicle carriers.
In comments to USTR, supporters of the pause argued that it would avoid higher shipping costs, prevent commercial disruptions and provide time for negotiations. Some sought permanent suspension of certain fees, warning that their return could disrupt trade and harm U.S. exports.
Opponents argued that the fees are needed to encourage investment in American shipbuilding and related industries, including container manufacturing. Some commenters also urged USTR to treat cargo-equipment tariffs separately from maritime service fees and end the suspension of those tariffs.
USTR said the United States will use the additional negotiating period to pursue its concerns with China while continuing efforts to expand domestic commercial shipbuilding capacity, develop the workforce and cooperate with allies.
Why it matters: The reciprocal pause averts additional shipping costs and potential disruptions affecting not only U.S. and Chinese carriers but also businesses worldwide that rely on Chinese-built vessels. It gives importers, exporters and shipowners temporary relief while trade negotiations continue.

articles.title_zh: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
articles.content_orig:
Tabletop provides customizable, collaborative spaces for all your personal planning needs.﻿
Tabletop provides customizable, collaborative spaces for all your personal planning needs.﻿
Google has cooked up a new experimental AI tool called Tabletop that generates customized collaborative hubs to help you coordinate with family, and friends. The Tabletop platform shares some visual similarities with workplace management apps like Asana and Monday, but with a built-in AI feature that allows you to vibecode personalized interactive tools by describing them, such as savings trackers, chore charts, event plans, and more.
“Just add in your links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets,” Google Labs design and engineering lead Roman Nurik said in the blog post. “Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time like a Google Doc.”
Access to the Tabletop beta is rolling out via a waitlist , and currently limited to people over the age of 18 in the US. Some of the example use cases that Nurik provides in his video above would clearly require giving kids or teens access to Tabletop, however, and using this for personal family planning looks like a compelling alternative to stuffy workplace software, so that age requirement might only be in place while Tabletop is in public testing.

This is CNBC's Morning Squawk newsletter. Subscribe here to receive future editions in your inbox.
Hello, this is Leonie Kidd with today's edition of Morning Squawk.
CoreWeave is providing the tailwind for futures today, helping lift neocloud stocks, while a rebound for Nvidia is also supporting the chip space.
But is it enough to dull the lingering doubts around the AI trade?
CoreWeave shares are surging in premarket trading, up over 16% overnight, after the neocloud group posted a 168% spike in third-quarter revenue.
The group also lifted its 2026 guidance , driving other neocloud stocks higher.
But bear in mind that shares are down 65% from their May highs, losing over 40% of their value in the last month alone.
Nvidia shares are extending gains in premarket trading, up just over 3%.
The move is also supporting gains for Broadcom , AMD , Intel and Nebius .
Here are the key developments:
CNBC's Seema Mody spoke to sources within Nvidia who said Huang walked into the group's Santa Clara, California, headquarters on Monday to hold his regular meeting with top-level executives.
To go inside that meeting, read the full piece here on CNBC.com.
Anthropic is offering 825 million shares at a price range of $70-78 per share.
Sources close to the deal told CNBC the AI titan is planning to price on November 18 and trade on November 19.
CNBC's Morning Squawk recaps the biggest stories investors should know before the stock market opens, every weekday morning.
Subscribe here to get access today .
The House of Representatives has effectively voted down an attempt to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The House, by a 211-204 margin, approved a measure that will refer the impeachment resolution to a committee, leaving little time for it to be acted on before Democrats take over in January.
Tokenization: The next evolution of the stock market
The U.S. equity market has repeatedly changed its underlying mechanics while the asset itself — a share of stock — has remained largely the same.
Trading moved from floors and phone calls to electronic venues. Settlement cycles compressed. Commissions fell to zero. Fractional shares and online brokerages expanded retail participation.
The next major change may already be underway.

articles.title_orig: Windows 11 KB5132061 KB5131087 November 2026 Patch Tuesday direct download links here
articles.title_zh: Windows 11 KB5132061 KB5131087 November 2026 Patch Tuesday direct download links here
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft is investigating reports of Windows 11 KB5132061 installation errors, including 0x800f0993, 0x80070306, and 0x800f0989. In our tests, we observed that the November 2026 Patch Tuesday update reaches 99% before it fails, and you won’t make any progress even if you reattempt the installation.
On November 10, Microsoft rolled out Windows 11 KB5132061 as part of this month’s Patch Tuesday cycle, which means it’s a mandatory security update with close to 700 critical Windows-specific security fixes, plus other improvements like a customizable right-click menu.
KB5132061 bumps Windows 11 26H2 to Build 26300.9974 and 25H2 to Build 26200.9974, and it’s supposed to take a few minutes to finish installing. Usually, a Windows update requires a single reboot, but this one may require two or more reboots because of a pending Windows Secure Boot certificate update.
Two or more reboots aren’t exactly a problem, but there’s a bug that’s preventing the November 2026 update from installing. On my PC, the update installed within a few minutes. But some users aren’t even able to get it to finish installing, and retrying doesn’t help.
“I’m stuck in a loop of installing KB5132061, but it’s repeatedly throwing errors such as 0x800f0993, 0x80070306, and 0x800f0989,” one user told Windows Latest, and there are dozens of similar complaints.
One user told us that the November 2026 update failed on four of their PCs with either 0x800f0989 or 0x80070306. They tried downloading the update manually and resetting Windows Update components, but it still failed.
Another user ran into 0x80070306 on two virtual machines and shared the following error:
“Installation Failure: Windows failed to install the following update with error 0x80070306: 2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300.9974).”
I’ve also seen reports of Windows 11 KB5132061 failing with 0x800f0993 and 0x800f0922. One person said it failed seven times, including once when they tried the offline installer from the Microsoft Update Catalog, before it finally installed on another attempt.
Of course, not everyone is affected. Some users have reported that the update installed without any errors, while others say it eventually went through after they restarted their PC and tried again.
Microsoft’s support document still says the company is “not currently aware of any issues with this update.” However, that doesn’t mean Microsoft isn’t looking at the reports, as I’ve been told the company is fully aware of the complaints and is investigating the root cause, including the possibility that Sandbox is responsible.
Windows Latest understands that Windows 11 KB5132061 installation issues could be tied to Windows Sandbox, so if you turn it off, you should be able to install the cumulative update without any trouble.
For those unaware, Windows Sandbox is one of the lesser-known features of Windows, and it lets you run apps in an isolated environment (virtual machine), with the idea of easily testing untrusted programs or downloads. It’s a great addition, and some might have turned on the feature without even realizing it, and now it’s causing the November 2026 update to fail.
One user who looked at their Windows installation logs noticed an error referring to a file used by Sandbox. On their PC, the update failed while Sandbox was enabled, but installed after they turned it off and restarted.
However, I’ve also seen a report from someone who ran into the error without having the option enabled. But if you use Sandbox and the update keeps failing, it might be worth trying:
If you just can’t get Windows 11 KB5132061 to install, you can also try downloading the update from the Microsoft Update Catalog .
If nothing else works, Windows 11 has a Fix problems using Windows Update option under Settings > System > Recovery . It’ll reinstall your current version of Windows while keeping your apps, files, and settings.
For now, Microsoft is looking into the reports, and we’ll update this article when we learn more.

His articles and research works have been referred to by CNN, Business Insiders, Forbes, Fortune, CBS Interactive, Microsoft and many others over the years.

articles.title_orig: Why Sandisk and Lumentum Are Leading the AI Comeback
articles.title_zh: Why Sandisk and Lumentum Are Leading the AI Comeback
articles.content_orig:
The Nasdaq Composite index briefly entered correction territory last week, dropping by more than 10% from its peak as the prices of artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks collapsed. Memory and storage giant Sandisk ( SNDK +15.81% ) has fallen 64% from its highs set only in June, after rising more than 10 times in value.
Sandisk management has scheduled a stock split to take place on Nov. 19. The flash memory maker trades at a cheap-looking price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) right now, but it just might be the most expensive stock you could buy today. Here's why I am not buying Sandisk stock despite the price dip and the upcoming stock split.
Image source: Getty Images.
Data storage giant Western Digital bought SanDisk in 2016, but then hived it back off (with a slightly different name) in early 2025. Since then, the rapid pace of the AI infrastructure build-out has driven a massive increase in demand and a deep worldwide shortage of memory chips. Because of that, Sandisk and its peers have been able to raise their prices sharply.
NASDAQ · As of 2:59 PM ET 11/11/26
Last quarter, its revenue was $11 billion, up 378% year over year, with a gross margin of 85%. Gross margin was below 30% in the same quarter a year ago. This boom has led to massive earnings growth, with $8.78 billion in earnings last quarter alone, up from barely breaking even a year prior.
That earnings inflection is why Sandisk stock was at one point up by more than 6,000% since Western Digital spun it off. Now, though, it has fallen by more than half from that peak in conjunction with the Nasdaq correction.
Many news items have accumulated since Sandisk's stock peaked in June that have caused investors to become nervous about the AI infrastructure theme.
OpenAI delayed its IPO. Neoclouds such as CoreWeave are reportedly having trouble raising funds in the debt markets. The midterm elections could have sweeping impacts on AI regulation and the pace of data center construction.
The less capital that flows into the AI companies, the less they will have to spend on memory chips from Sandisk. This narrative has taken hold of Wall Street at the moment, and it's why Sandisk stock has been falling.
When Sandisk reported its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results on Oct. 29, management guided for sequential revenue growth of around 10% in its fiscal Q2. This suggests that memory demand continues to grow, but that would be slower than fiscal Q1's 23% sequential growth. Wall Street hates slowing revenue growth.
SNDK Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts .
Sandisk and its peers are all in the midst of building new facilities to manufacture more memory and grab more of the growing market. But eventually, as that additional production comes online in the quarters and years ahead, the supply of memory chips will come back in balance with demand. It may then exceed demand, creating a glut, at which point Sandisk and its cohort will run into trouble.
Sandisk's ability to implement significant price increases across its product lines over the past year and a half has led to massive earnings growth. The sharp shift in its gross margins illustrates the wild cyclicality in the memory chip market. Historically, the memory chip sector has experienced many periods of high demand and prices that were followed by equally deep declines as the supply-and-demand dynamic reversed. I don't think this time will be different.
For investors, the stock split is a meaningless event. It only increases the total number of shares outstanding , but it changes nothing about either the stock's valuation or the underlying business. Never buy shares in a company just because of a stock split.
Right now, Sandisk trades at what looks like a dirt-cheap forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) of 3.5. It is possible that Sandisk will generate the expected level of earnings that ratio is based on over the next 12 months. However, over a longer time horizon, a downturn in the memory chip market could significantly affect this earnings ratio.
If Sandisk's annualized revenues fall back to $10 billion (which is what the company was reporting less than a year ago) and its operating margin collapses from 73% to 10% as it loses its shortage-driven pricing power, its earnings will fall to $1 billion. That would give it a P/E ratio of 100 relative to the current market cap of around $100 billion. That makes Sandisk stock look wildly expensive for anyone thinking about holding it beyond the next few quarters.

articles.title_orig: JetBlue unveils new first class seats to bring back profits
articles.title_zh: JetBlue unveils new first class seats to bring back profits
articles.content_orig:
JetBlue Airways is unveiling its new domestic first-class seats Wednesday as more of the country's carriers bet on the premium travel boom to make them profitable again.
JetBlue announced it would offer a domestic first class — BlueFirst — in December 2024 and plans to start flying aircraft with the new seats and full on-board product next month. The carrier is showing off the new cabin at its home hub at John F. Kennedy International Airport on Wednesday. Retrofits will continue during 2027, CEO Joanna Geraghty told CNBC late last month.
The rollout comes as the New York airline tries to stabilize after last posting a profit in 2019. Last month, JetBlue executives sought to calm investors after shares in the airline hit a record low following a report that bondholders had contracted restructuring advisors.
"We have no intention, no plans to file for bankruptcy. We are not engaged with any restructuring company," Geraghty told CNBC in an interview on Oct. 27.
Geraghty told CNBC's Phil LeBeau on Wednesday that JetBlue has "met with a few of the creditors over the last couple of weeks as part of ... normal investor engagement." She said the company made it clear to bondholders that JetBlue doesn't need to reorganize.
The airline's shares are up more than 40% this month, more than other passenger carriers, as of midday Wednesday, though they are still off about 11% so far this year.
JetBlue is betting that resilient travel demand, especially for for roomier seats will help fuel its turnaround plan, which aims to get the carrier to an operating profit next year and $1 in adjusted earnings per share in 2028.
Airline executives have said they expect fares to stay elevated next year as they grapple with higher costs, including but not limited to fuel, such as labor and airport fees. Geraghty said Wednesday that even if fuel prices moderate next year, "I don't think fares are going to fall as much as people expect."
Airlines large and small are racing to outfit their cabins with roomier, more expensive seating options to help cover ever-higher costs, from jet fuel to labor to airport operation fees.
For example, a ticket in the new recliner first-class seats between Kennedy Airport and Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport in Florida is going for $847 roundtrip in the first week of March while standard economy is $446.
On Tuesday, budget carrier Frontier Airlines unveiled its new first class seats, which will take up the first two rows, and said it would outfit its Airbus fleet with premium seating that have extra legroom and in-seat power through row eight. The airline will take out a row of seating on its planes to make the pricier ones fit, chief marketing officer Bobby Schroeter told CNBC in an interview Monday.
JetBlue last month reported it ended the third quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity and that its unencumbered asset base is now $7 billion, including $2.8 billion in aircraft and engines.
JetBlue had total debt of $8.4 billion as of Sept. 30, the carrier said in its earnings filing.
Geraghty told CNBC last month there is a "fundamental disconnect between the narrative in the bond market and what our financial results actually demonstrate."
When asked then whether JetBlue's eye on keeping costs down includes furloughs, layoffs or buyouts, Geraghty last month said "absolutely not."

articles.title_orig: USPS Warns of Major Changes to Post Offices and Mail Delivery
articles.title_zh: USPS Warns of Major Changes to Post Offices and Mail Delivery
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. Postal Service is in severe financial disarray and will be forced to make drastic cuts unless Congress intervenes to save it, the agency has warned.
In a statement released on Tuesday, USPS reported losses of $6.5 billion over the course of the fiscal year. Although the figure is an improvement on last year’s loss of $9 billion, the continued financial drain is starting to have a serious effect on the agency’s ability to operate.
“We will need to make drastic changes in the number of post offices and marketing mail service levels,” said Postmaster General David Steiner. “And we will need to look at other areas to generate the cash we need to meet our obligations to our employees and to the American public.”
Steiner said the scale of the problem requires immediate Congressional action, “as the uncontrollable costs of our retirement plans continue to create an untenable situation for our employees.”
Congress has two options to consider, he added: Either remove the retirement mandates that prevent the agency from running as a self-sustaining business, or provide the additional funding to allow it to overcome the financial deficit.
If neither of these options are considered, both Congress and the American public will have to accept substantial cuts to its services, Steiner warned.
“The USPS is the core of a nearly $2 trillion ecosystem, supporting almost 8 million jobs, and providing critical infrastructure that reaches every address in the country,” he said. “Any financial support to cover the shortfall would be an investment in one of the central pillars of the U.S. economy.”
Steiner previously appealed to lawmakers for additional funding back in June, warning the House that the agency could run out of funds within months unless action is taken.
"The bottom line is that we are out of cash. We are borrowing from our employees’ retirement funds to continue operations," he told the Senate during a committee hearing. "The Postal Service has a broken business model and action is needed by Congress to fix it."
USPS has been reporting net losses of around $120 billion since 2007, after its biggest money-maker, first-class mail, saw a sharp decrease in usage following the shift to digital communications.
The Postal Service delivers to 170 million addresses six days a week, costing the agency $3.4 billion a year, Steiner said. Seventy percent of routes lose money, and around 58 percent of its 18,000 post offices are also unprofitable.
Last year saw Steiner’s predecessor, Louis DeJoy, strike a deal with the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) to eliminate 10,000 jobs at the Postal Service in an attempt to trim down the agency’s deficit; a move that likely had a significant impact on the reduced losses reported by USPS on Tuesday. The move, however, was sharply criticized by labor unions and congressional Democrats, with House Representative Gerald Connolly stating the move would have “catastrophic consequences for all Americans.”
Steiner’s comments come three months after he previously warned lawmakers that postal deliveries may halt in 2027 due to a lack of funds. However, following a series of emergency measures, including a temporary price hike in April to cover rising fuel costs and a multi-year deal with DHL, the agency is now suspected to stay afloat until at least 2031.
“Ultimately, our fiscal cliff is here,”  USPS Governor Amber McReynolds told Politico. “The board continues to make uncomfortable default decisions, and we do not want to continue to operate in an unsustainable position as we have.”
The USPS will now look to the new Democrat-controlled Congress for next steps when the new intake assumes their seats in January.
President Donald Trump has previously floated the idea of either privatizing the Postal Service or merging it with the Department of Commerce. However, the move has been strongly opposed by workers, with a survey by the American Postal Workers Union showing those surveyed rejecting privatization by a margin of 34 percent.
“Plans to privatize the Post Office are about enriching Wall Street and not serving Main Street,” said APWU President Mark Dimondstein. “Evidence shows that selling off the USPS would lead to higher prices for postal services as well as higher prices for shipping packages at FedEx and UPS.”

articles.title_orig: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
articles.title_zh: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
articles.content_orig:
DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment.
DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment.
Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease — and point the way to new treatments.
AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year . While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells — from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection — switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change depending on what a cell is doing. As a result, the same genetic variant can have very different effects depending on the type and state of the cell.
The new model is designed to capture those differences, predicting the effects of genetic variants on individual cell types and states. Google said in a blog post published Wednesday that it offers a much finer-grained view than broader models like AlphaGenome, potentially revealing disease-relevant effects in specific cells that might otherwise go unnoticed.
AlphaGenome 2 was trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues to give it that more detailed view. DeepMind says the model effectively turns static cell atlases — huge data repositories that map and catalog individual cells in detail — “into a predictive engine for human genetics.” According to the company, AlphaGenome 2 identifies nearly twice as many variants that can change gene expression in cells than its previous state-of-the-art model.
Notably, the researchers found that AlphaGenome 2 could also make predictions about new types of cells and biological states without needing to be retrained. It could also identify gaps in experimental data, potentially helping scientists decide what to investigate next in the lab.
For Adam Gayoso, a research scientist at Google DeepMind involved in the project, the big breakthrough is “tying human genetics to cell biology.” AlphaGenome 2 gives researchers a way to drill down on genetic variants identified in large populations, to see what effects they may be having on a cellular level, and potentially connect those effects to disease, he told The Verge .
Google DeepMind’s genomics lead Žiga Avsec told The Verge that this specificity is important if you have a goal like figuring out how to treat a particular disease. “When you develop drugs, you’re targeting specific proteins and specific cell types,” he explained, which makes having this kind of granularity vital.
Building a model like AlphaGenome 2 has only recently become possible thanks to new technologies that can capture individual cells and their states at high resolution and create the vast datasets needed to train it, Avsec said. DeepMind is now working to improve its genetics models by generating more data, including for cell states that aren’t represented well today. Avsec said future versions could also potentially be trained on data “across multiple species,” giving the models a broader view of biology. Longer term, he said models like AlphaGenome 2 could feed into efforts to create “ virtual cells ,” digital simulations designed to mimic biological systems.
Although Avsec said he views AlphaGenome 2 as a successor to AlphaGenome, it isn’t replacing it any time soon. He said its more detailed predictions come at a computational cost and are “more expensive” to produce than those of its predecessor, he said. Those demands would have made it impractical to use AlphaGenome 2 to produce the genome-wide Atlas covering “every possible DNA letter change in the human genome” that DeepMind released in September.
Google says it is making AlphaGenome 2 available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API from today, with a limited “private preview” for commercial research.
The model is the latest in a growing array of efforts by Google and rival AI labs to use the technology to tackle major problems in science and medicine. Pushmeet Kohli, who heads DeepMind’s AI for science research, has hinted that more impressive scientific results are on the way, and the organization is expected to open an automated materials science lab in the UK soon. Anthropic, meanwhile, has been experimenting with drug design and given Claude a wet lab , while OpenAI has been mowing down an impressive amount of longstanding problems in mathematics and related fields .

NVIDIA Corporation ’s ( NVDA Quick Quote NVDA - Free Report )     latest pullback amid the CEO Jensen Huang controversy has sparked fresh concerns among investors. But does the stock decline offer a buying opportunity, given the company’s strong financial performance and growth outlook? Let’s take a closer look –
Co-founded by Jensen Huang in 1993, NVIDIA has grown into a tech behemoth, banking on the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Beyond running a successful business, Huang has emerged as an influential voice in Washington. However, his reputation, along with NVIDIA’s shares, came under pressure recently after he admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Since the controversy surfaced, NVIDIA stock has plummeted nearly 10% and erased almost $430 billion in market capitalization over the past two trading sessions. Investors were already concerned about the potential impact of geopolitical tensions, regulatory scrutiny and uncertainty over AI spending on NVIDIA’s growth trajectory, and the latest controversy has now raised new concerns about the company’s reputation.
Despite the controversy, NVIDIA’s long-term growth prospects remain strong, driven by sustained demand for cutting-edge AI chips, data-center infrastructure, and advanced computing. NVIDIA’s powerful graphics processing units ecosystem and proprietary CUDA software have given it a competitive edge in powering the next phase of AI innovation.
Management remains quite confident that its revenue growth momentum will remain strong. NVIDIA expects fiscal third-quarter 2027 revenues to be $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, up from $96 billion reported in the fiscal second quarter of 2027, which marked 106% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter growth, according to the company’s Aug. 26 press release.
The Data Center business remains the primary growth driver, with revenues jumping 117% to $89 billion in the fiscal second quarter. As NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform has entered full production, the company is well-poised to tap the strong demand for AI infrastructure and sustain revenue growth.
Alongside revenues, NVIDIA’s profitability also improved. Its gross margins have risen to 75% in the fiscal second quarter from 72.4% a year earlier, alongside improvements in operating income, highlighting NVIDIA’s strong financial performance.
Investors should look beyond short-term reputational risks and concentrate more on NVIDIA’s strong AI-driven growth trajectory and robust financials. The company continues to report strong quarterly results, driven by accelerating data center growth, and has provided upbeat guidance.
Moreover, Huang’s leadership and long-term vision no doubt matter significantly, but NVIDIA’s strong market position and talent pool ensure that its fate is not entirely dependent on one individual. Nonetheless, the controversy-led sell-off offers investors an opportunity to buy NVIDIA’s shares at a lower valuation. It has a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 18.16 compared to the Semiconductor - General industry’s 21.52.

articles.title_orig: Kidnapper, 74, escapes from house arrest in Argentina by abseiling from balcony
articles.title_zh: Kidnapper, 74, escapes from house arrest in Argentina by abseiling from balcony
articles.content_orig:
Leonardo Bertulazzi was first arrested in Buenos Aires in 2002
A 74-year-old Italian man who was found guilty of a kidnapping carried out by a far-left militant group in the 1970s has escaped while under house arrest in Argentina and is on the run.
Leonardo Bertulazzi used a harness to abseil down from a fifth-floor balcony in the capital, Buenos Aires.
His escape was not immediately registered because he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor so that it continued to transmit body temperature measurements even after he had prised it open and absconded.
Bertulazzi already spent decades as a fugitive after he was sentenced in absentia in Italy for the 1977 kidnapping of Italian naval engineer Pietro Costa.
He was awaiting extradition to Italy and was being monitored by the Argentine ministry of security through an ankle tag which registers the wearer's body temperature and movements.
Officials said that they had become suspicious when they noticed that the tag had remained stationary.
When they entered the fifth-floor apartment in the centre of Buenos Aires, Bertulazzi was gone, but the ankle monitor remained.
Wary of Bertulazzi's past with the Marxist guerilla group the Red Brigades and his bomb-making skills, police called in explosives experts in case it had been rigged to detonate, according to Argentine newspaper ClarÃ­n.
However, the experts found that while Bertulazzi had tampered with the device, he had done so to prevent the alarm from sounding once he removed it.
A nationwide manhunt is now under way.
Italian media say that his extradition to Italy had been imminent after his last appeal was rejected.
Bertulazzi was first arrested after using a false passport to cross into Argentina from neighbouring Chile in 2002.
However, he was granted refugee status in 2004 and lived freely in the South American country until his re-arrest in 2024, when the current right-wing president, Javier Milei, took office.
Milei's government said at the time that "Bertulazzi is responsible for crimes that undermined democratic values and the lives of many victims".
He was a member of the Red Brigades, which kidnapped and killed a number of state officials in the 1970s and '80s.
Bertulazzi was part of the Red Brigades' Genoa section that kidnapped Pietro Costa on the street and then held him for 81 days before receiving a big ransom.
The money it made from the kidnapping was then used to buy a flat in Rome, which was used in 1978 for the Red Brigades' most notorious crime, the kidnap and murder of Italian former Prime Minister, Aldo Moro.
Moro was abducted when his car was ambushed on the way to the opening of parliament. He was held in the flat for 54 days before he was shot and his body abandoned in the boot of a Renault car in the centre of Rome.

articles.title_orig: Iran-US deal faces major hurdles as Tehran refuses uranium transfer
articles.title_zh: Iran-US deal faces major hurdles as Tehran refuses uranium transfer
articles.content_orig:
Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, the main mediator between the US and Iran, has acknowledged in closed-door discussions that the gaps between Iran and the United States remain significant.
However, he added, Qatar and the other mediators are working to bridge those differences, two sources familiar with the details told The Jerusalem Post .
It is already clear that any potential agreement will be implemented in stages rather than through immediate, simultaneous steps. As a result, beyond the substance of the measures themselves, one of the key points of contention is the sequencing of those steps and which side will make the first move.
One of the reasons for Al Thani’s meeting with President Donald Trump at the White House on Monday was to reassure the Iranians that the US president genuinely wants to reach an agreement, a source familiar with the details said.
On Wednesday, Trump said: “The United States has won [the war]. It’s just a question of when we stop. We want to win 100%, not 90-something percent.”
Al Thani told G7 foreign ministers on Tuesday that Trump is currently allowing roughly two weeks for diplomatic efforts to exhaust all possibilities for reaching an agreement.
This comes after Iranian Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei said that the Islamic Republic will not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country, and there will be consequences in the event of any new US strikes.
Rezaei was speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV after US officials downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.
Rezaei has said there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran and Washington .
"Any new US attacks will also be met with targeting US bases far away," he warned, referring to bases beyond the scope of the previous war.
The security chief was explicit in his warning, saying that military bases in European countries would be attacked should US aircraft launch attacks on Iran from them.
Iran's Supreme Leader has issued a directive that the country's near-weapons-grade uranium should not be sent abroad, two senior Iranian sources said in May.
"We need the enriched material to design ships and submarines that work on nuclear energy", Rezaei said, adding that Tehran has informed Moscow that its enriched nuclear material will remain in the country and "we will use it ourselves".
Russia has previously offered to remove uranium from Iran as part of a potential deal to ease US concerns but said it was for Tehran to decide whether to remove it or not.
The IAEA estimates that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% - a level far higher than needed for civilian use - when Israel and the US attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much of that ⁠has survived is ​unclear.
Israel, the United States and other Western countries have long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons. Iran denies the accusation.
Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the war between the two countries .
Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets seven demands which Tehran has presented, a senior Iranian official told Reuters last week.
Jonah Davidov contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo returns to Peru, his adopted homeland
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo returns to Peru, his adopted homeland
articles.content_orig:
Lee el artículo en español
Riding on horseback to visit the most isolated Andean areas of his community, distributing food amid the Covid-19 pandemic, or wearing rubber boots in the water and mud of floods: this is how many Peruvians remember the man who is now Pope Leo XIV.
Robert Prevost was in the trenches and alongside his people during Peru’s most difficult moments, and many of these memories will likely be front of mind among the public as they welcome the pope on his visit to his adopted homeland on Wednesday.
The pope’s visit to Peru, which will include visits to Lima, Cusco and Chiclayo, is widely seen as a homecoming for a pontiff who is a Peruvian citizen and who knows the country in depth.
A young Prevost first arrived in the South American country as a missionary in 1985. The years that followed shaped his leadership style, which would later lead him to become the successor to the late Pope Francis.
“I think he was heroic in many ways; he risked becoming ill. We lost 11 priests and a bishop emeritus during that time,” Father José Del Rosario recalls of the most difficult days of the pandemic.
Padre Robert, as he is known in Spanish in Peru, traveled more than 700 kilometers (435 miles) from Chiclayo to the Diocese of Callao, a province bordering the capital, Lima, where he served as apostolic administrator.
“He came every two weeks in his little car; he came alone in a simple pickup truck,” explained Del Rosario, parish priest and rector of the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Mount Carmel of La Legua, who worked closely with the then-bishop.
Pope! Amigo! Peruvians remember the young American priest who became pope
Prevost distributed food and everything needed by a population that lived under lockdown for months, while also offering spiritual guidance during the crisis.
“He gave us a lot of hope and cared for our people, a man who was very close to the people … and also very humble,” Del Rosario added.
Peru recorded more than 219,000 deaths , according to Johns Hopkins University figures, and one of the highest coronavirus mortality rates in the world. In Lima, and especially in the regions, terrifying scenes unfolded outside hospitals, with sick people collapsing in the street due to the shortage of oxygen, one of the key tools for treating the virus.
In Chiclayo, Bishop Prevost launched a fundraising campaign to purchase an oxygen plant. Together with Caritas Chiclayo, the bishop appealed to authorities and sectors of civil society and managed to raise more than US$380,000 for not just one but two oxygen plants.
Janinna Sesa, former director of Caritas Chiclayo, worked with the bishop for eight years, including during the pandemic, the flooding caused by the coastal El Niño in 2017, and Cyclone Yaku in 2023.
“We were always on the front lines, especially during disasters like the coastal El Niño phenomenon. He was the person who put on his boots and waded into the water; he helped people. He was very approachable and very kind,” Sesa told CNN.
Before leaving for Rome in 2023, after the late Pope Francis appointed him prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops and president of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America, Bishop Prevost also led appeals for aid for the more than 10,000 people affected by flooding caused by Cyclone Yaku in the north of the country.
“I ask you to be generous; I ask you to open your hearts so that we can help one another and move forward, as we have done in other times of crisis,” Prevost said in a video while standing in the water in the district of Illimo, in the Lambayeque region.
The assistance and response led by Prevost in the face of the massive arrival of Venezuelan migrants in 2018 was comprehensive and had a different vision from that of the country’s other regions.
Peru received more than 1.6 million Venezuelans through November 2025, the second-highest number in the region after Colombia. More than 20,000 of them passed through Chiclayo, and more than 3,500 families settled in the region, according to figures from the Commission for Human Mobility and Human Trafficking of the Diocese of Chiclayo. Prevost also promoted this commission to assist migrants and combat human trafficking.
First American pope marks July 4 on migrant island with plea for ‘compassion and generosity’
“The migration flow descended upon us, with thousands of migrants out on the streets, sleeping there, and the parishes serving as shelters,” Sesa recalled.
Father Robert was concerned not only with providing food and collecting clothing, blankets, and medicine, but also with building the San Vicente de Paúl village, which took them in at Puerto Etén.
“His simplicity, the peace he conveys, that serenity Monsignor Prevost had when listening to people — I still see it in Pope Leo XIV…. He welcomed us with such warmth, with so much love,” Lisbeth Díaz, a Venezuelan resident of Chiclayo and member of the Commission for Human Mobility and Human Trafficking, told CNN.
Prevost prioritized regularizing their legal status so they could work and integrate into society.
Prevost created spaces for dialogue and encouraged many people to raise their voices to denounce abuses during the internal conflict the country experienced beginning in the 1980s and to openly discuss the social reality during the authoritarian regime of the late President Alberto Fujimori in the 1990s.
At the Augustinian mission in Trujillo, the current pontiff and his seminarians traveled through towns and parishes in Andean areas, staging dramatizations that reflected the violence faced by peasants to encourage conversations that would help heal the trauma and pain they had suffered.
Prevost also participated in collecting signatures for the creation of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC), which investigated the violence between 1980 and 2000 and human rights abuses, particularly in rural Peru. Trujillo and the parishes led by the current pontiff collected the largest number of signatures.
Leo XIV is a pope forged in Peru. The nearly two decades he spent in the land he adopted as his own profoundly shaped his ministry and set him on the path to the papacy. As a bishop, Prevost was a pastor close to his flock, and at the Vatican, one of his closest collaborators is the Reverend Edgard Rimaycuna, a native of Chiclayo.
His work in South America and his leadership of the Order of Saint Augustine caught the attention of Pope Francis, who first appointed him bishop of Chiclayo and later brought him to Rome, where he went on to hold one of the most important positions in the Vatican and also became a cardinal. This made him a candidate in the 2025 conclave.
Pope Leo presides at biggest Mass of his papacy in Buenos Aires, drawing 2.5 million crowd
In the past, the election of an American pope was considered impossible, given that the College of Cardinals did not wish to associate the papacy with the dominant political and cultural power. However, the cardinals who voted for Cardinal Robert Prevost in the 2025 conclave did not see him simply as a candidate from the United States.
His experience in Peru garnered broad consensus among the cardinals, who chose a bishop with roots in Latin America — someone who speaks Spanish fluently and is attuned to the concerns of the people of that continent.
The pope’s visit to Peru will be an opportunity for the Peruvian people to welcome Padre Robert back to the adopted country that shaped him — and that he shaped deeply as well.
Reverend John Lydon, a priest and member of the same Augustinian religious order to which the pope belongs, and who lived and worked with Prevost for a decade, told CNN: “I believe his dedication to the poor and his defense of human rights will continue to define his visit.”

articles.title_orig: AWS Emulator and the engineer's job when agents write the code
articles.title_zh: AWS Emulator and the engineer's job when agents write the code
articles.content_orig:
AWS launched a new local emulator service for its cloud services on Wednesday to help enterprises accelerate application development and testing.
The service, named AWS Emulator, will allow developers and AI coding agents to build, deploy, and test AWS-dependent applications on their machines without provisioning actual cloud infrastructure and paying for it, thereby potentially reducing development time and associated costs, the hyperscaler said in a statement.
To achieve this, AWS Emulator replicates the APIs of AWS services locally and exposes a local HTTP endpoint that the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), software development kits (SDKs), and coding agents can access using the same APIs they use to interact with the cloud, it added.
Developers can redirect these tools to the local endpoint by setting the AWS_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable, allowing existing application code and tests to run against simulated AWS services without modification, it further said.
The new service addresses a growing problem for developers in software development: the need to test increasingly complex cloud applications quickly and repeatedly without the cost and operational overhead of deploying them to the cloud, said Ashish Chaturvedi , executive research leader at HFS Research.
“Developers can test multi-service workflows involving S3 , Lambda , DynamoDB , and API Gateway without provisioning anything, and they avoid both the AWS charges and the clutter of half-finished resources that experiments tend to leave behind in shared accounts,” Chaturvedi said.
“I am sure there would be clients that found a forgotten test bucket or idle instance on a cloud bill months later. Such clients will appreciate an environment that vanishes when the work is done,” Chaturvedi added.
The bigger advantage of the service, however, will be for developers using AI coding agents, according to Advait Patel , senior site reliability engineer (SRE) at Broadcom.
“Agents work in loops: write code, run it, see the error, fix it, repeat. When every loop hits real AWS, you wait on provisioning, you pay for resources, and you clean up whatever the agent forgot to delete. Moving that loop to a laptop cuts each cycle from minutes to seconds,” Patel said.
“Teams get faster feedback, fewer leftover test resources, and smaller dev account bills. It also means you can let an agent try things freely without worrying about it spinning up something expensive in a real account,” Patel added.
That combination of reduced operational overhead and costs, in turn, is likely to appeal to CIOs looking to accelerate software delivery and scale AI-assisted engineering across their organizations, according to Chaturvedi.
“The clearest benefit is cycle time. Faster feedback in the inner development loop shortens delivery, and that compounds across hundreds or thousands of developers, especially as AI-assisted engineering spreads,” Chaturvedi said.
“The less obvious benefit is safer agent adoption. Many CIOs hesitate to let coding agents provision infrastructure because one misstep in a real account can be costly or create a security exposure. A local environment where agents can experiment freely gives organizations a way to scale AI-assisted engineering while keeping agents away from real resources until the code has been tested,” Chaturvedi added.
Despite its potential to accelerate development and testing, AWS Emulator comes with limitations that could prevent enterprises from relying on it as a substitute for testing applications against actual cloud infrastructure, according to Devin Pratt , research director at IDC.
“At launch, the emulator does not simulate throttling or outages, snapshot and restore, or per-Region availability, which matter most for resilience,” Pratt said.
And these gaps, according to Patel, “are the ones that cause real outages.”
“From an SRE view, throttling, partial failures, and regional differences are exactly what take systems down in production. If your tests never see a 429 or a timeout, your retry and backoff logic never gets tested. So yes, there is a real risk of false confidence, especially if teams start treating ‘passed locally’ as ‘ready to ship’ status,” Patel said.
More so because AWS’s own fidelity measurements indicate that the emulator does not yet reproduce every AWS operation accurately.
The hyperscaler measures the fidelity of the service by comparing API responses with those from actual AWS services and testing whether multi-step workflows behave as expected. Operations that have not been implemented or verified return HTTP 503 errors rather than being treated as successful, it said.
That distinction is important because successful tests against the emulator do not necessarily guarantee that applications will behave identically when deployed on actual AWS infrastructure, Patel said.
Developers will therefore need to validate their applications against real cloud environments before deploying them to production, Patel added.
There are security concerns as well, particularly because the emulator does not sandbox the code it executes, according to Pratt.
This means that if developers include real production credentials in functions being tested locally, the code could still access actual AWS resources, potentially exposing enterprises to unintended resource access or security risks, Pratt said.
Despite these trade-offs, enterprises looking to adopt the service can download the Emulator at no charge, with the tool available for Linux, macOS, and Windows, and its source code published on GitHub, the hyperscaler said.
Currently, the emulator supports all 426 AWS services and is built using Rust to minimize CPU and memory consumption, with support for new services and API changes following updates to AWS’ published interface models, it added.

articles.title_orig: Crude Futures Pick Up After Heavy Selling
articles.title_zh: Crude Futures Pick Up After Heavy Selling
articles.content_orig:
International oil benchmark Brent crude briefly fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August on Tuesday as comments from U.S. President Donald Trump fueled hopes for an end to Washington's nearly nine-month conflict with Iran.
Brent, the price gauge for around 80% of global crude, settled down 1.17% at $91.49 a barrel. At its session low, the international benchmark slid to $89.16. U.S. WTI crude fell 0.93% to settle at $86.04 a barrel.
Trump said on Monday that the war with Iran could end "fairly soon" and that Tehran was "talking very politely" with Washington.
"We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," he said at the White House following a meeting with Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani. "Iran militarily is effectively over," Trump told reporters.
Trump also said in a Truth Social post that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait would "prefer the status quo," namely maintaining a naval blockade against Iran and preventing the country from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials.
Crude oil prices have been highly volatile this year, proving sensitive to any perceived shift in direction in the U.S. and Israel's war with Iran.
Brent crude started the year around $60 a barrel before soaring as high as $130 a barrel as military strikes escalated in March and April. Prices retreated in June and July before climbing back to those levels as the conflict increasingly appeared entrenched.
Crude oil flows through the key Strait of Hormuz waterway have largely recovered . But consumers have suffered from resulting volatility in energy markets, as wider global conflicts — including Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the Russia-Ukraine war — exacerbate a shortage of refining capacity, sending prices of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel soaring.
Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both acknowledged that public disapproval of the Iran war and high energy prices played a role in the Republicans' punishing result in the U.S. midterms last week .
While officials on both sides have continued to trade hostile words, particularly as they debate control of the Strait of Hormuz , the U.S. had largely held back on military strikes since September, with Trump saying in early October they would not resume until after the midterms.
The U.S. carried out what Trump called "minor strikes" on Iran after reports that two missiles struck Qeshm Island, located near the Strait of Hormuz off the country's southern coast.
Analysts were divided on how the U.S. administration would approach the Iran conflict after the Democrats' resounding midterm victories, with some viewing escalation as a strong possibility despite the initial market reaction suggesting hopes of a deal.
"The market has continued to unwind some of the geopolitical risk premium built into prices in recent weeks as expectations grow that the conflict between the US and Iran could move towards de-escalation," ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson said in a note Tuesday.
"Signs that regional oil flows are recovering have added to the downward pressure... Reports that Iran may be softening its position on control of the Strait of Hormuz have also reduced concerns over a prolonged disruption to one of the world's most important oil transit routes."
"For now, the return of more Gulf barrels and the prospect of easing tensions are taking some of the geopolitical premium out of crude. However, with regional negotiations still uncertain and infrastructure risks persisting, we expect oil prices to remain sensitive to developments in the Middle East."
Fereidun Fesharaki, chairman of energy consultancy FGE, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Tuesday that, despite market moves, he still did not see any prospects of a peace deal between the U.S. and Iran.
"The difference between the two sides is so wide, it cannot be bridged. Most importantly, the U.S. wants all the nuclear material, enriched material, to be transferred out of Iran, and there is no way that the Iranian regime would agree to this, and there is no way the Iranian regime would agree to let the Strait of Hormuz be open for a free flow of oil the way it was before the war," Fesharaki said.
"So, with these two in between, I just can't see a deal being made.
"Trump has to decide. Either he says, 'I declare victory and walk away,' or he goes to war. If he goes to war, he's got only a window of two weeks from today for himself and for [Israeli Prime Minister] Netanyahu, or there will be no war at all on a long-term basis," Fesharaki added.
Netanyahu's political party failed to win a majority in Israel's election last month, with rival Gadi Eisenkot, the former chief of the Israel Defense Forces, officially tasked with forming a government on Sunday.
— CNBC's Anniek Bao contributed to this story.
Correction: An earlier version of this story misstated the session low for Brent crude.

articles.title_orig: Thousands of hoax bomb alerts sent to schools in Italy, U.K. and Ireland
articles.title_zh: Thousands of hoax bomb alerts sent to schools in Italy, U.K. and Ireland
articles.content_orig:
Schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday ⁠after around 6,300 of them received bomb warnings, the latest in a series of threats and cyberattacks around Europe against supermarkets , blood banks, air traffic and broadcasters.
Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland said many of their schools received a similar email threat from abroad but it was classed as a hoax and did not disrupt classes.
In Italy, schools closed swiftly after ⁠the warnings, prompting many parents to drop what they were ​doing ⁠to collect children.
“My daughter Dafne started crying because the kids did not understand what was happening, and she was still shaken when I picked her up,” said Nensi Bego, parent of a child ⁠at the Mazzini middle school in Rome.
“This is so annoying. It’s obvious it’s just a hoax that disrupts ​lessons and ⁠disrupts everyone’s day.”
A copy of the ‌message seen by Reuters also included a threat to target Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni . She said the bomb alerts posed no danger and that police and other public bodies were monitoring the situation.
“All students have been taken ‌to a safe area and remain under the supervision of teaching ‌staff,” one school in Rome informed parents through a messaging app.
The email received in Italy was signed “Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan,” according to a copy of the message seen by Reuters.
“The (school) emails are public. (Sending the bomb alert messages) was as easy as drinking a ⁠glass of water,” a national security source told Reuters.
The same purported author claimed responsibility for email bomb threats sent on Friday to newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria.
Some European officials suspect Russia may be behind a campaign of disruption to everyday life in European nations supporting Ukraine after Moscow’s invasion.
Russia denies that and accuses the West of a smear campaign.
Iran is another suspect. France summoned Iran’s ambassador on Tuesday after accusing Tehran of a cyberattack that disabled refrigerators in hundreds of supermarkets last week.
Iran rejected those accusations as “baseless and hostile”.
Italian ‌Defense Minister Guido Crosetto said Wednesday’s threats were part of a clear strategy “to spread fear and ​create anxiety,” according to Adnkronos news agency.
“It is not always the work of foreign countries ‌or hostile entities. There are also attention-seekers and lunatics ⁠who, at a time like this, cannot wait to unleash terror in a city or a region,” ⁠he added.
Antonello Giannelli, head of the Italian School Principals Association, said the alerts were upsetting for students, families and school staff.
“Even though today’s ‌threats are clearly hoaxes, we cannot underestimate ​the consequences of incidents that alarm entire school communities ‌and disrupt the normal conduct of educational activities,” he ​said.

articles.content_orig:
Tuesday, November 10, 2026 9:00AM
MIAMI BEACH, Fla. — November 10, 2026 — Today at Adobe MAX — the world's largest creativity conference — Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) — the global technology leader that unleashes creativity, productivity and customer experiences through innovative tools and platforms — announced innovations that transform Creative Cloud tools into agentic workflows, built with the precision and control pros expect, giving creatives more time for their craft. The Adobe Creative Agent is expanding across Creative Cloud, orchestrating multi-step workflows so creative professionals can delegate and direct work, increasing their creative velocity. Adobe also previewed the local MCP integrations that will allow pros to use Creative Cloud tools from their preferred third-party agents.
New Creative Cloud innovations, including Generative Restyle in Photoshop , Color Mode in Premiere and Co-editing in InDesign , help photographers, video editors and designers work faster and with greater precision. Adobe also introduced Firefly Design (beta), which brings raster, vector, motion, 3D and print together on one canvas so designers can create, review and deliver their work all in one place. Following Adobe’s acquisition, Topaz Labs is introducing two new image enhancement models, Wonder 4 and Image HDR delivering upscaling, denoising, deblurring and sharpening capabilities to transform images with richer detail.
Creative professionals are increasingly working across more mediums, apps and formats, while facing growing demand to deliver high-quality work faster. Adobe is advancing a new approach to creating that brings AI assistance and collaboration directly into the Adobe tools they rely on, helping them move from idea to execution faster and with greater flexibility, precision and control. Creative professionals remain in control throughout the process, choosing when to delegate tasks to AI, when to make hands-on adjustments and how to apply their perspective, taste and judgment to shape the final result.
“The ideas, taste, style and vision that creative professionals bring to their work are what make their work stand out,” said Deepa Subramaniam, vice president, product marketing, Creative Cloud at Adobe. “Our latest Creative Cloud innovations transform our trusted creative tools into agentic, intelligent workflows that give pros the precision, control and flexibility to explore their ideas, streamline their work and stay focused on the creative decisions that make their work uniquely theirs.”
The Adobe Creative Agent is now available in flagship desktop tools including Premiere , Illustrator , InDesign , After Effects and Frame.io . This brings more creative professionals a creative partner that orchestrates multi-step workflows behind the scenes, putting them in the director’s chair so they can stay focused on their craft. The Creative Agent now supports new capabilities in Premiere including applying effects across every clip in a sequence, tracking masked subjects through a frame, and adjusting color and exposure across an entire sequence at once.
Adobe is also previewing local MCP integrations for Creative Cloud tools that will let creative professionals direct their preferred third-party agents to work locally in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects, with the agent making changes directly in native project files on the user’s computer. Layers, vectors, bins and sequences remain editable, and creative professionals can step in at any moment to refine the work by hand. If the agent is also connected to other MCP-capable tools such as Google Drive or Slack, it can bring them into the same workflow, pulling in a brief from Google Docs, working on the project with Adobe’s tools and sharing the result with colleagues in Slack.
Creative work increasingly spans image , video , audio and design to bring projects to life. Adobe Firefly , the AI creative studio, brings Adobe’s industry-leading creative tools, top industry AI models and the Adobe Creative Agent together in one place, with the power and precision creative professionals need. When pros want to go deeper, they can seamlessly move into Creative Cloud tools to further refine their work.
New capabilities in Adobe Firefly include:
Adobe is introducing new editing tools and performance enhancements across Creative Cloud to help creative professionals tackle complex tasks faster, refine their work with greater precision and advance their craft. New innovations include:
Following Adobe’s acquisition of Topaz Labs , a leader in AI-powered image and video enhancement technology, the company is introducing two new image enhancement models, Wonder 4 and Image HDR , giving creative professionals even more power to enhance and refine their images. Powered by a first-of-its-kind Mixture of Experts architecture, Wonder 4 is an image enhancement model that combines upscaling, denoising, deblurring, sharpening, and more, to transform images with a single click. Image HDR uses AI to transforms standard images into HDR, enhancing brightness and creating richer details. The latest capabilities empower photographers, retouchers and designers to recover images that might otherwise have been set aside and deliver more polished visuals in less time, freeing them to spend more time capturing new images or bringing their photos into new creative projects.
New capabilities in Creative Cloud are generally available today. Co-editing in InDesign, Open Eyes in Lightroom and Firefly Design, Firefly Graph are available in beta. Firefly Builder is currently in private beta.
AI Assistants powered by the Adobe Creative Agent are available in beta in Adobe’s flagship desktop apps, except Photoshop where the AI Assistant is available in the Photoshop beta app. Topaz models are available to purchase here . Adobe’s local MCP integrations for Creative Cloud tools will be available in private beta in early 2027.

articles.title_orig: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
articles.title_zh: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
articles.content_orig:
Lina Attalah has said Egypt is "trying to limit the already-limited space" for independent media
A criminal court in Cairo has postponed the retrial of the prominent Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, whose case has drawn international condemnation.
Wednesday's opening hearing was adjourned until 18 November after defence lawyers representing the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr requested a new judge.
The UN has warned of "widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities, including the targeting, persecution and harassment of independent journalists".
Attalah told the BBC that a recent crackdown was meant to "send a chilling message" to "the very few newsrooms that are left".
She warned: "Everybody should be careful, everybody should be scared, everybody should be wondering if they are next."
Set up 13 years ago, Mada Masr became Egypt's leading independent news site with Attalah as its editor-in-chief and co-founder.
Last month, the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court convicted her of running a website without a licence - which she said she had tried in vain for years to obtain. She was issued a hefty fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds ($56,000; Â£42,000) and Mada Masr was ordered to shut down.
After that trial, Attalah found that a court had previously given her a one-year prison sentence, without her knowledge, for "spreading false news" - a charge often used against journalists and dissidents - as well as operating a website without a licence. It was issued in absentia in 2024, even though she was in the country at the time. Attalah is now being retried in that case by the same judge.
At the opening session, Attalah's defence team requested the judge's recusal, arguing that he had "already formed a conviction in mind against the defendant", Mada Masr cited its lawyer Hassan al-Azhar as saying , external . The judge went into recess before adjourning proceedings for a week to allow the court to consider the defence's request, he added.
Mada Masr also said Attalah's appeal against last month's conviction was scheduled to take place on 25 November.
Egypt has largely stifled freedom of the press, ranking 169th out of 180 countries for press freedom, according to Reporters Without Borders' 2026 analysis. The group says that at least 26 journalists who were arrested in recent years remain in detention.
While most newspapers and television stations now keep to government lines, Mada Masr remained a rare, independent and investigative news source in Egypt. However, since 2017 the site could only be viewed from outside the country.
It had reported on alleged corruption and human rights abuses, and provided deep coverage of politics and economics, as well as regional upheaval and wars in Libya, Sudan and Gaza.
In her BBC interview on Sunday, Attalah insisted that the factual reporting and professional standards of Mada Masr had an important role to play in Egyptian society, which could benefit the government.
"It's much better if you have a little space left to have it open for professional media organisations who do rigorous reporting, because if we disappear, then you make the space for conspiracies and disinformation," she said.
"People need to know, people need to consume information and you're shooting yourself in the foot if you're killing the newsrooms that do it properly."
In September, six journalists with the independent fact-checking platform, Matsda2sh - constituting its entire newsroom - were arrested in home raids by the Egyptian authorities and held incommunicado for nearly a week.
Six journalists working for the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh are facing terrorism charges
They have since been charged with joining the Muslim Brotherhood and financing terrorism, and their lawyers report that several were beaten and electrocuted in detention. They say that no evidence has been presented linking them to the Brotherhood.
Egypt's former president Mohammed Morsi â who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood â was removed from power by the military, led by Abdul Fattah al-Sisi, in July 2013 after widespread protests. Under Sisi, who became president the following year, the Islamist movement was classed as a terrorist organisation, leading to a widespread clampdown.
On Tuesday, a spokesperson for the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Thameen Al-Kheetan, called for the Matsda2sh reporters to be released, with all charges dropped.
He also said the case against Attalah "raises fresh concerns regarding due process and fair trial".
"We call on Egypt to end all forms of harassment of journalists and media outlets, and to respect and fulfil the right to freedom of expression, including the right to information," Al-Kheetan said.
"The steps taken to suppress the continued work of both Matsda2sh and Mada Masr must be overturned. The people of Egypt have a right to read and hear views expressed through these fora on issues of legitimate public concern."
Attalah has suggested the authorities might again be trying to silence independent voices at a time of economic strain in Egypt and regional instability.
It has been widely noted that recent legal action against journalists comes after the US State Department waived human rights conditions on $320m (Â£240m) in its foreign military funding for Egypt in September. This allowed the funds to be released as part of Washington's annual $1.3bn military aid package.
The BBC asked US Secretary of State Marco Rubio whether he had raised the recent crackdown on independent journalism with Egypt's Foreign Minister, Badr Abdelatty, at their meeting about regional tensions in Paris on Monday.
"We didn't discuss it today," Rubio said. "Butâ¦ like anything else in foreign policy, there's always a balancing act to further the national interest of the United States. And in the end, Egypt has been a reliable and good defence partner of the United States."
"That doesn't mean you agree with everything another government does," he went on, adding that he was not "opining about their journalists".
